hero.kicker: Commercial snow removal and grounds care in Grand Blanc, MI
hero.title: One call for **the lot and the lawn.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes plows and salts parking lots, drives and walks for businesses, HOAs, churches, offices and apartment and senior communities, then mows and keeps the same grounds when the snow is gone. Rob walks the property with you and quotes the parts you need.

blocks.title: Snow and grounds, **one contact.**
body: A commercial property needs two things from a grounds company: snow and ice handled through the winter, and the grounds kept the rest of the year. Grand Scapes does both, so a manager or a board has one name to call instead of two. You deal with Rob directly, by phone or text.

Before the season, Rob walks the lot with you. He looks at the entrances, the parking rows, the walks and doorways, where the snow can be piled without eating parking or blocking a driver's view, and which spots ice over first. Then he explains the options and quotes it.

items.title: Businesses and offices
items.body: The lot, the entrance and the walk to the door are what customers and staff see first. Those get plowed and treated in winter, and the lawn out front gets mowed and edged in summer.

items.title: HOAs
items.body: Entrances, common areas and shared walks can be plowed in winter and mowed in summer on one plan. The board or the manager gets one contact for both seasons.

items.title: Churches
items.body: Lots, walks and steps need to be clear on the days people come. Tell Rob your service and event schedule when he walks the property, and he will talk through how that is handled.

items.title: Apartment and senior communities
items.body: Walks, steps and drop off areas matter most where residents walk with care. Rob looks at every entrance and talks through how the walks and the ice are handled.

blocks.title: From the walk around to **the season.**

steps.title: Walk the property
steps.body: Rob walks the lot with you or your board: entrances, parking rows, walks, steps, dumpster pads and the places snow can be piled.

steps.title: Mark the edges
steps.body: Curbs, islands and drive edges need marking before the ground freezes, so a plow can find them under snow. Rob goes over what needs a stake.

steps.title: Snow season
steps.body: Our trucks plow the lot and drives, walks and entrances are cleared, and ice melt goes down where people walk and cars stop.

steps.title: Grounds season
steps.body: When the snow is gone, we do the [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup/), then mow, trim, edge and blow off the grounds through the season, and take the leaves away in fall.

blocks.footnote: Rob explains how a commercial season is quoted when he walks the property. We do not publish prices or terms, because every lot is different.

blocks.title: Snow belongs **on your side of the curb.**
body: Michigan's vehicle code, MCL 257.677a, says a person shall not deposit snow, ice or slush on any roadway or highway. It also bars putting snow onto a road or its shoulder in a way that blocks a driver's view, and a violation is a civil infraction. For a lot that opens onto a busy road, that decides where the piles go.

The public streets are plowed by priority. The Genesee County Road Commission says expressways come first, then main streets, then local roads, with subdivision streets last, and that it cannot give a time for any one street. Your lot, your drives and your walks are on you. That is the part we handle, in Grand Blanc and in towns like [Flint](/commercial-snow-removal-flint-mi/), [Burton](/commercial-snow-removal-burton-mi/) and [Fenton](/commercial-snow-removal-fenton-mi/).

faq.q: Do you do commercial snow removal in Grand Blanc?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes plows and salts parking lots, drives and walks for businesses, HOAs, churches, offices and apartment and senior communities in Grand Blanc and across Genesee County, with our own trucks. Call or text Rob at [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) to set up a walk around.

faq.q: Can one company handle our snow and our lawn?
faq.a: Yes. We plow and salt in winter, and mow, trim, edge and clean up the grounds the rest of the year, so a property manager or board has one contact for both. Rob quotes the parts you need.
Yes. Entrances, common areas and shared walks can be plowed and salted in winter and mowed and kept in summer. Rob will walk the community with the board or the manager and explain the options.

faq.q: How is commercial snow removal priced?
faq.a: Every lot is different, so Rob walks it first: the size, the entrances, the walks, where the snow can go and how the property is used. Then he explains the options and quotes it, and the estimate is free. We do not publish prices.

faq.q: Where do you put the snow from a parking lot?
faq.a: On the property, in spots Rob picks with you on the walk around: away from entrances and the parking you need, and never in the road. Michigan law, MCL 257.677a, bars depositing snow on a roadway, and piles should not block a driver's view of the road.

faq.q: Do you salt walks and entrances?
faq.a: Yes. Walks, steps and entrances are cleared and treated with ice melt where people walk and cars stop. Rock salt slows down sharply below about 15 degrees Fahrenheit, so very cold days are part of the conversation. More on our [salting and sidewalks](/salting-and-sidewalks/) page.

faq.q: Do you do commercial work in Flint and Burton?
faq.a: Yes. We take commercial work across Genesee County, including [Flint](/commercial-snow-removal-flint-mi/), [Burton](/commercial-snow-removal-burton-mi/), [Flint Township](/commercial-snow-removal-flint-township-mi/), [Fenton](/commercial-snow-removal-fenton-mi/) and [Davison](/commercial-snow-removal-davison-mi/). Call or text Rob to talk about your property.
